⚠️ Research Writing Series - Day 10 ⚠️
How to Write DISCUSSION Part
✦ for Systematic Literature Review

Purpose: To interpret the findings, explain their meaning, compare with existing knowledge and highlight implications for research and practice.

• Structure of Discussion
① Restate Main Findings
• Briefly remind the key results of your review.
② Interpret the Findings
• Explain what the results mean in the context of your research question.
③ Compare with Existing Literature
• Show how your findings agree, differ or extend earlier studies.
④ Identify Patterns, Themes & Relationships
• Highlight major trends, gaps, contradictions or inconsistencies.
⑤ Explain Possible Reasons
• Discuss why these findings may have occurred.
⑥ Implications
• Theoretical, Practical, Policy and Social implications.
⑦ Limitations of the Review
• Acknowledge limitations in included studies and in your review process.
⑧ Future Research Directions
• Suggest areas that need further exploration.

Writing Tips
* Don't just repeat results – interpret them.
* Use evidence from included studies to support your points.
* Be critical but balanced.
* Link back to your research question and objectives.
* Use strong transitions and logical flow.
* End with a clear take-home message.

Useful Phrases
• The findings suggest that...
• This result is consistent with...
• In contrast, some studies found...
• This difference may be due to...
• These findings imply...
• This review highlights the need for...

Quick Checklist
☐ Have I answered my research question?
☐ Have I interpreted the main findings?
☐ Have I compared with existing studies?
☐ Have I discussed implications?
☐ Have I mentioned limitations?
☐ Have I suggested future directions?

★ Take-away: A strong Discussion explains the "WHY" behind the findings and shows their "SIGNIFICANCE".

——— ♥ Good Discussion = Strong Impact! ♥ ———
